label: wrapped asset conversion
summary: Plan a hook that converts between an underlying and wrapped or staked representation with exact rates, rounding, custody, and exits.
requiredFacts: Exact underlying and wrapped asset identities, conversion entry points, rate source, decimals, rounding and minimum output
Whether wrapping or unwrapping can pause, queue, revert, charge fees, rebase, upgrade, blocklist or depend on an oracle
Which callback performs conversion and how its deltas, custody, native value, refunds and self-calls settle to zero
Canonical PoolKey, router and quoter behavior with byte-identical hookData and the same conversion assumptions
Direct user exit and recovery path when conversion or the external wrapper is unavailable
requiredFiles: Pinned wrapper and hook source closure
Rate, rounding, fee and solvency specification
App quote, swap and disclosure integration
Executable wrapper failure and exit tests
requiredTests: Rate movement, zero and boundary amounts, decimals, rounding, fee, rebase and stale quote
All swap quadrants, partial fills, native value, Permit2, refunds, hookData and final deltas
Wrapper pause, queue, blocklist, upgrade, insolvency, malicious return value and dependency outage
Direct and routed wrapping, unwrapping, self-calls, nested actions and reentrancy
User exit, recovery and no cross-pool or cross-asset liability leakage
risks: A wrapped or staked token can add issuer, upgrade, redemption, oracle and legal risks absent from the underlying
Quote and execution can diverge when conversion rates or fees change in the same block
Rounding and mixed native or ERC-20 settlement can create unbacked deltas or trapped dust
